blocks.text: Dear Ms. Banks:

I am writing to record, with as much care as I can bring to it, the terms on which our firm would undertake the commercial due diligence you and your colleagues have asked us to perform, so that once you have read this letter and, finding that it captures the understanding we reached in our recent conversations, returned a signed copy to me, there exists a single document to which either of us can turn should a question later arise about what was agreed. I have tried throughout to commit us only to what I am confident we can deliver, and should any passage below read as promising more than that, I would ask you to raise it with me before you sign, so that nothing in the letter outruns what we can actually do.
The Question You Have Put to Us

As we understand it, {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} is weighing a decision in which the commercial standing of the business under review matters more than any single figure on its financial statements, and you have asked us to examine that standing from the outside and to report on it plainly. Our work will take in the market the business serves and the direction and pace at which that market is moving, the position the business holds within it and the durability of that position against its competitors, the composition and loyalty of its customers, and the quality and repeatability of the revenue it reports, so that you can enter your decision knowing where the commercial case is genuinely strong and where it rests on assumptions that will not bear their weight. What the engagement does not take in is a view on the accounting, the tax exposure, or the legal terms of any transaction, on which you should continue to rely on the advisers who ordinarily provide it; where our analysis touches those matters we will offer a reasoned commercial judgment and not a professional opinion in their place.
How We Intend to Work

Our method is deliberate, and I hope you will find it plain rather than clever. We begin by assembling the evidence patiently and reconciling it against itself before we draw a single conclusion from it, so that every judgment we eventually put in front of you can be traced back to the source beneath it and questioned there if you wish. Where the evidence will support a firm view we will give you one, and where it will support only a range or a caution we will tell you so instead, because a conclusion that runs past what we actually know is of no use to you and no credit to us, and a commercial due diligence earns its keep precisely at the points where it declines to overstate.
Who Will Do the Work

I will keep my own hand on the engagement and read anything of consequence before it leaves us under the firm's name, but the daily work will rest with three of our people whom I would ask you to come to know. Melissa Casey will build the exhibits on which the findings rest and hold the status pack consistent from one week to the next, keeping every chart tied to the source beneath it. Cynthia Hart will carry the industry and competitive research, reading widely across the public record and distilling what she finds into short, sourced summaries. Nicole Griffin will gather and keep in order the source material the analysis runs on, from public filings to the notes taken in our working sessions, so that no figure we show you is ever unmoored from where it came from. You are welcome to reach me at any time, though for most day-to-day matters Melissa Casey will be the quicker route to an answer.
Fee and Start

Our fee for the engagement as I have described it is {{fact:f:E-2015-001.fee}}, which covers the time of the people named above through the completion of the work and against which we will render invoices as the engagement proceeds. We would begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}}, and would move promptly into the first information requests and interviews after that, so that the opening weeks are not lost to arranging what could have been settled in advance.
Rendering and Payment of Invoices

Each invoice we render against the fee stated above is payable within thirty days of your receipt of it. The fee covers our people and their time, and not the incidental costs of the work, such as travel or the purchase of third-party market data, which we will incur only with your agreement and pass through to you at what they cost us and nothing more. Should the shape of the work change materially from what this letter contemplates, I will raise the fee with you and we will settle it together before any further work is done, so that nothing ever reaches you on an invoice as a surprise.
Term and Termination

We expect the engagement to run for something on the order of seven months, though I would ask you to treat that as an honest estimate of the work rather than a promise about the calendar, since we will regard the assignment as finished when it is genuinely done and not merely when a set number of weeks has passed. Either of us may bring the engagement to an end on thirty days' written notice to the other, and should you choose to do so you would owe us for the work properly performed to that point and for any costs already committed on your behalf, and for nothing beyond that.
Confidentiality

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} and about the business under review in the course of this work we will hold in confidence and use only for the purposes of the engagement. That obligation binds every member of the team, it outlasts the end of our work together, and it covers the fact of our involvement as fully as it covers its substance. We would ask the same of you in respect of the methods and written materials we share, which are the firm's own way of working and are meant for your use rather than for wider circulation.
Limitation of Liability

We will perform the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of a firm engaged for it, and we stand behind what we do. We do not, however, control the commercial decision that {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} will ultimately take on the strength of our advice, nor the conditions in which that decision is carried out, and so, save to the extent the law does not permit such a limit, our liability to you arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute arising under it will be determined by the courts of that state. Should any single provision of this letter be held unenforceable, the remainder will stand, unaffected by it.

If this letter reflects the understanding we reached, I would be grateful if you would sign the enclosed copy where indicated below and return it to me, keeping the second copy for your own file; once your signed copy is in hand, Melissa Casey will write to arrange the opening interviews and the first requests for information, so that we lose none of the early weeks to settling what can be settled now.

The engagement opens on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}}, and this memo sets down how we begin so that the three of us are in step from the first day. The aim of the opening weeks is narrow and worth stating plainly: we assemble a clean, sourced base of evidence on the market and on the business under review, and we form no commercial judgment yet. Nothing we produce in this phase is a conclusion; it is the foundation the later analysis stands on, and it has to be solid before we build anything on it.
The opening weeks

items: Market and demand. Size the market the business serves and establish the direction and pace at which it is moving, with every figure tied to a named source rather than to a recollection.
Competitive position. Map the principal competitors and the position the business holds among them, and mark where that position looks durable and where it looks exposed.
Customers and revenue. Assemble what the public record shows of the customer base and the composition of revenue, and note plainly where the record thins out, so we know what to ask the client for.
Source discipline. Keep every chart and table tied to its source from the first draft, so that no exhibit ever reaches a status pack unsourced and no citation has to be chased after the fact.

blocks.text: Cynthia Hart will take the market and competitive reading, since that is the desk work she does best, and Nicole Griffin will keep the source library in order so that neither of you rebuilds a document the other has already pulled. I will hold the exhibit templates and the running status pack, and I would ask that anything meant for a client-facing page reach me with its source attached, because an unsourced exhibit is an unfinished one and I would rather settle the citation while it is still fresh.

Our sponsor on the client side is Barbara Banks, the Chief Operating Officer, and every request for data or access should route through her so that {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} hears a single voice from us. Set the context of a request in a sentence before you make it, so she can see why we are asking, and plan the requests together rather than send them piecemeal as they occur to us.

Two dependencies will set the pace of these weeks. The first is the reach of the public record, which will carry the market and competitive reading a long way but will thin out on the customer and revenue detail, where we will have to lean on what Barbara Banks's team can give us. The second is the freshness of the trade sources we rely on; where a source is dated, mark it as such on the exhibit rather than let its age go unrecorded, and flag it to me the moment it looks material.

The first step is the consolidated information request. Draft it between you by the end of next week and send it to me, and I will fold in the client contacts and the exhibit numbering before it goes out. Once that is in Barbara Banks's hands we can begin the market reading in earnest, and the two of you should hold a short standing check-in with me each week so that anything blocked surfaces early rather than at a review.
Dear Barbara,

A short note on where the commercial due diligence stands. Cynthia Hart has the market and competitive reading substantially in hand for the two segments that matter most, and Nicole Griffin has assembled the public filings and the trade sources sitting behind it, so the base of evidence is coming together as we planned. None of it is a conclusion yet; it is the ground the later commercial judgment will rest on.

To close the picture I need two things from your side. The first is the internal customer and revenue detail we flagged in our opening request, so that the public record can be checked against your own numbers rather than left to stand on its own. The second is thirty minutes each with two of your commercial managers, since the texture behind the revenue tends to live with the people who carry the accounts. If any of that needs a sign-off above your desk, Barbara Banks, point me to the right person and I will approach them directly rather than add to your own load.

Send whatever is easiest straight to me, Melissa Casey, and I will keep this thread as the single place these requests and their answers live. If the customer detail reaches us by the middle of next week, we stay comfortably on track for {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}.
Sincerely
Record of a Working Session

These minutes record the working session held on the commercial due diligence for {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}, at which the engagement team and the client reviewed the evidence gathered so far and settled which questions the second half of the work should take up. They set down who was present, what was discussed, and the actions each side agreed to carry before we meet again.
Present

items: Nicole Griffin, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners (minutes)
Melissa Casey, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners
Cynthia Hart, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners

blocks.text: Discussion

Cynthia Hart walked the group through the market and competitive reading, which is now substantially complete for the two largest segments and under way on the rest. Her account was that the market is growing steadily rather than sharply, and that the business under review holds a defensible position in its core segment but a thinner one at the edges, where two larger competitors have been gaining. Nicole Griffin noted where each figure in the reading traces back, so that the client could see the sourcing rather than take the conclusions on trust.

We then turned to the customers and the revenue, where the public record has taken us only so far. Melissa Casey set out the exhibits she has built to date and was careful to mark, on each one, the point at which the external evidence gives out and the client's own numbers would have to carry the analysis further. Barbara Banks confirmed that the internal customer detail can be made available, and observed from her own vantage that a handful of the largest accounts sit behind a disproportionate share of revenue, which is the sort of concentration the diligence exists to test rather than to assume.

One question we left open by agreement, since it belongs to a later stage of the work. The team can either press the competitive reading deeper into the two adjacent segments, which is the more thorough course, or hold the segment map where it is and put the freed time into the revenue-quality analysis, which is the more pointed one. No one pressed for a decision in the room, because the choice turns on what the internal customer detail shows once we have it, and we agreed to settle it at the next session rather than guess at it now.
Actions

rows: Assemble and send the internal customer and revenue detail against our opening request
Close the competitive reading on the two remaining segments and record the sources
Reconcile the public revenue picture against the internal numbers once received, and flag any gap on the exhibits

blocks.text: The item that gates our next session is the first action, since until the internal customer detail is in hand we cannot reconcile the revenue picture or settle the open question above; once Barbara Banks's team has sent it, I will circulate the updated exhibits ahead of the meeting so that no one reads them cold.
Commercial Due Diligence: Status Report

This report sets out where the commercial due diligence for {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} stands at the midpoint of the engagement, what the team has completed since the work began, what remains ahead of us, and the risks worth watching between now and the close. The work is on schedule and is being delivered within the agreed fee of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.fee}}, and nothing in the evidence gathered so far has forced a change to the scope set out in the engagement letter.

The team has held to its planned cadence of working sessions with your office, and the shared engagement file now holds a single sourced record that your own people will be able to work from after we have gone. I have written this report to be read on its own, so that a colleague who has not sat in the sessions can take the state of the work from it without a briefing.
Where Things Stand

The base of external evidence on the market, the competitive field, and the customer picture is now substantially in place, and the analysis has moved from gathering to testing. The picture that is emerging is a favorable but qualified one: a durable position in the core segment, set against a thinner position at the edges and a concentration of revenue among a small number of large accounts.

None of these reads as a settled conclusion yet, because each turns in part on internal detail that your team is now assembling for us. The value of the second half of the engagement lies precisely in closing that gap, so that what we finally put in front of you rests on your own numbers rather than on the public record's approximation of them.
Completed This Period

items: Cynthia Hart completed the market sizing and the competitive reading for the two largest segments, each figure traced to a named source.
Nicole Griffin assembled and organized the public filings and trade sources, so that the shared engagement file holds a single ordered record the team works from.
Melissa Casey built the customer and revenue exhibits and marked on each the point at which the external evidence gives out and the client's own numbers must carry the analysis on.

The team held its scheduled working session with your office, at which the current read was walked through segment by segment and the open questions for the second half were agreed rather than deferred.

blocks.text: The Weeks Ahead

The next phase reconciles the external picture against the internal customer and revenue detail your team is preparing, which is where the revenue-quality question is genuinely settled rather than estimated. In parallel, Cynthia Hart will close the competitive reading on the two remaining segments so that the segment map is complete before we draw the findings together.

Once the internal detail is in hand and reconciled, we expect to bring a first integrated read of the commercial case to a working session, framed as a set of findings you can take apart before any of them is treated as settled. The closing weeks after that go to the write-up and to stress-testing the two or three judgments the commercial case turns on, so that the final report distinguishes clearly between what the evidence establishes and what it only suggests.
Risks and Watch Items

Two items carry the schedule, and I would rather set them down now than have either surface late. The first is the timing of the internal customer detail: the revenue-quality analysis cannot close until it arrives, and a week of delay there is a week the phase does not move, so the sooner your team can release it the more comfortably we hold the finish.

The second is the revenue concentration itself, which the external record only hints at and which the internal numbers will either confirm or soften. It is the single point on which the commercial case most depends, and until we have reconciled it against your own accounts we are holding it open deliberately rather than reporting it as resolved.
Prepared by Melissa Casey, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners.

In Attendance

items: Nicole Griffin, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners (minutes)
Melissa Casey, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners
Cynthia Hart, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners

blocks.text: Matters Discussed

Melissa Casey walked the group through the integrated read, now that the internal customer and revenue detail has been reconciled against the external picture. The reconciliation held together more cleanly than we had feared: the internal numbers confirmed the durable position in the core segment and, on the concentration of revenue, softened the external read somewhat, since several of the largest accounts proved to sit under long-standing contracts rather than on year-to-year terms. Cynthia Hart added that the competitive reading on the two remaining segments is now closed, which completes the segment map that the earlier sessions had left partial.

We spent most of the hour on how firmly the findings can be stated, which is the judgment the whole engagement has been building toward. Nicole Griffin confirmed that every figure in the draft exhibits now traces to a source in the shared file, so that the client's own people will be able to rerun the analysis after we have gone. Barbara Banks asked that the final report distinguish clearly between what the evidence establishes and what it merely suggests, and the team agreed, since a due diligence that dresses a suggestion as a finding is worth less than one that marks the line honestly.

One matter we settled rather than left open. The team had earlier weighed pressing the competitive reading deeper against putting that time into the revenue-quality work; with the revenue question now largely answered by the internal detail, we agreed to hold the segment map where it stands and to spend the closing weeks on the write-up and on stress-testing the two or three judgments the commercial case turns on, rather than on further gathering.
Actions Agreed

rows: Draft the integrated findings and circulate the exhibits for team review
Stress-test the core-segment and revenue-concentration judgments against the reconciled numbers
Confirm the contract terms behind the largest accounts and note any exceptions for the record

blocks.text: The item that gates delivery is the first action, since the draft findings are what the closing review and the final report are both built on; once Melissa Casey has circulated them, Nicole Griffin will check every exhibit back to its source one last time before anything goes to the client under the firm's name.
